ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all Ultimate Beneficial Owners, directors, and authorized signatories against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, United States OFAC SDN List, United Kingdom HM Treasury Sanctions List, Interpol Red Notices, and the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade sanctions and designations lists maintained under the United Nations Act 1946 and Russia Sanctions Act 2022; enhanced due diligence applies to Politically Exposed Persons under section 22A of the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 consistent with FATF Recommendations 10–12 and the 2022 FATF Risk-Based Approach guidance for online gaming and digital app-based products; all screening records must be retained for at least five years after the termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office and New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) Register at https://www.companiesoffice.govt.nz; online name availability check via the Companies Office Name Search portal.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Entity names must use Latin alphabetic characters; Te Reo Māori names and macron or diacritical marks are permitted when they can be correctly entered into the NZBN system; the name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered, reserved, or protected name on the New Zealand Register under section 20 of the Companies Act 1993 and the Companies (Name Registration) Regulations 2016; the name must end with 'Limited' or the approved abbreviation 'Ltd'; the name must not falsely imply Crown, government, municipal, or professional association sponsorship, and must not contain offensive content or content that would constitute a criminal offence.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Companies Office refuses a proposed name at the name-approval stage under section 20(3) of the Companies Act 1993, the applicant may file a written Reconsideration Request with the Companies Office within 20 working days of the refusal decision, setting out grounds of non-confusing similarity, bona fide business intent, prior-user declarations, and any consent letters from affected rights holders; the Registrar must issue a reconsideration determination within 20 working days; a subsequent refusal may be appealed to the High Court of New Zealand under section 21 of the Companies Act 1993 and the High Court Rules 2016 by way of judicial review, with the appeal application to be filed within 20 working days after the Registrar's final decision; a previously reserved name may be preserved by filing a fresh reservation application before the expiry of the currently valid reservation period.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible as the registered office address only if it is a physical street address within New Zealand (not a P.O. Box), is staffed during ordinary business hours, and is operated by a registered agent or corporate service provider authorized to accept service of process on the company's behalf; the company must maintain its statutory records at a New Zealand location under sections 189 and 213 of the Companies Act 1993; for this digital MMORPG publishing business (ISIC 5820), the virtual office with agent presence satisfies the statutory mandate, but Apple App Store Connect and Google Play Console contract requirements and acquiring-bank AML due diligence may require additional evidence of operational substance such as director availability, service agreements, and local management infrastructure.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low, estimated at approximately 10% in the first 12 months for a Low_Risk_Standard, non-gambling, non-licensed digital publisher; the probability increases to approximately 35% if the company relies on the tax-exempt regime, fails to file an annual return, triggers an AML suspicious-transaction report, or becomes subject to payment-rail disputes with Apple or Google.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), in particular ss 10 (Constitution), 12 (Registration of Company), 13 (Date of Incorporation), 14 (Company Name), 16 (Registered Office), 17 (Address for Service), 22 (Approval of Certain Names), 25 (Objection to Name), 86 and 92 (Registers), and 122–128 (Officers and Consents); Companies (Forms) Regulations 2016; Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 (disclosure regime, where relevant).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), Wellington, New Zealand (operating the Companies Register online portal).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form NZ 1 – Application for Registration of a Company (electronic filing through the New Zealand Companies Register; accompanied by Form NZ 7 for registered office and Form NZ 8 for director consents).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account requirement under New Zealand law. The Company may be validly incorporated with one ordinary share issued at NZD 1.00 nominal value, fully or partly unpaid, subject to board resolution and subscriber consent.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED - RESOLVED, pursuant to the Companies Act 1993 and the Company Constitution adopted on this date, as follows: 1. The Company Constitution presented to this meeting is unconditionally adopted as the supreme governance instrument. 2. The Board allots and subscribes 1,000 fully paid ordinary shares of no par value to the initial shareholder for aggregate consideration of NZD 1,000, which has been satisfied to the satisfaction of the Board. 3. The registered office of the Company shall be situated at the address set out in the incorporation application, and the Company Secretary is authorised to file Form NZ 7 with the Registrar of Companies. 4. The following officers are appointed: [Full Name] as sole Director, [Full Name] as Chief Executive Officer, and [Full Name] as Company Secretary, each having executed signed consent to act. 5. The Board authorises procurement of the New Zealand Business Number, Inland Revenue IRD number, GST registration, and corporate banking facilities. 6. The Board ratifies negotiations with Apple App Store and Google Play for global distribution of the Company's MMORPG titles, including in-app purchase payout terms. No further business; meeting adjourned.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Search, Restricted-Name Approval and Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office – Companies Register (online name search and approval portal).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a corporate name availability search on the NZ Companies Register to confirm the proposed name 'CK International Company Limited' is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name. As the word 'International' is a restricted word under s 22 Companies Act 1993, file a written Application for Approval of Name with supporting justification of the Company's global MMORPG publishing scope. Upon approval, reserve the name for up to 20 business days and secure written consent of the directors and initial shareholder to use the name.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name search result
Application for Approval of Restricted Company Name (s 22 Companies Act 1993)
Directors' and initial shareholder's signed consents to use the name
Supporting business description evidencing global software-publishing scope
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, amend the application to a distinctive alternative name or register the company using its company number until a new name is approved. The applicant may object under s 25 Companies Act 1993 within 20 business days of refusal and, if necessary, pursue judicial review in the High Court of New Zealand.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Constitution and Corporate Governance Package
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand incorporated law firm / notary public; subsequent filing with the New Zealand Companies Office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Company Constitution under s 10 Companies Act 1993, adopting standard CANZ governance powers including share transfer provisions, director indemnity consistent with s 162, and special-resolution amendment procedures. Prepare the subscriber statement, share allotment documentation, and the first board resolution. Execute and notarize the constitution and obtain signed statutory consents from each proposed director.
required_dossiers: Company Constitution executed by all subscribers
Subscription agreement and share application form
Consent to act as director (Form NZ 8 statutory consent)
First Board Resolution minutes
Directors' identification documents (RealMe or passports)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office queries inconsistent constitutional clauses, revise the constitution and file a substituted copy. Any provision conflicting with the Companies Act 1993 is automatically void under s 34, and the Board may adopt a replacement provision within 30 days to maintain governance continuity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Submission of Form NZ 1 Incorporation Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office – Companies Register online portal (www.companiesoffice.govt.nz).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into the Companies Register and complete the online incorporation application. Enter the full legal name, registered office, address for service, director and shareholder particulars, and share structure. Attach the reserved-name approval and the executed constitution. Each director must verify identity through RealMe with a passport or internationally accepted identity document. Pay the NZD 150.00 government registration fee by credit card or online banking and submit the application. The Certificate of Incorporation is issued electronically upon successful registration.
required_dossiers: Form NZ 1 – Application for Registration of a Company
Approved company name reservation (if restricted word used)
Executed Company Constitution
RealMe-verified identity records for all directors
Shareholder and director consents
Form NZ 7 registered office consent executed by the office provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a notice of proposed refusal under s 12(5) owing to incomplete particulars, the applicant must correct the defects and resubmit within the statutory window, normally 20 business days. Upon final refusal, the applicant may appeal to the High Court pursuant to s 12(9) Companies Act 1993.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Business Registration (NZBN, IRD, GST and PAYE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) via the Companies Office; Inland Revenue – Business Registration portal (myIR).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation, the Company automatically obtains a New Zealand Business Number and a provisional IRD number by data exchange. Log into the Inland Revenue business registration portal and activate the IRD number, elect GST registration (compulsory where annual taxable supplies exceed NZD 60,000; optional in the initial low-revenue phase), and register PAYE/RWT if officers receive salary. Provide the corporate bank account details for GST refunds and dividend imputation election if future distributions are contemplated.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Directors' passports or RealMe identity verification
NZBN confirmation letter
Corporate bank account details
IRD business registration election (IR360 self-service)
Projected revenue statement from MMORPG in-app purchase model
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD number is not automatically issued within 3 working days, file paper form IR596 with the Companies Office incorporation certificate. If the GST registration is questioned, furnish projected annual revenue figures; where uncertainty persists, the Company may seek a binding ruling under s 91C Tax Administration Act 1994.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Formalisation of Registered Office and Officer Appointments (Forms NZ 7 and NZ 8)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office – Companies Register.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form NZ 7 declaring the registered office and address for service, and Form NZ 8 recording the appointment of all directors, together with signed consents to act. Ensure the company registers and maintains its share register and director register at the registered office or an approved registers office as required by ss 86 and 92 Companies Act 1993. Complete the Ultimate Beneficial Ownership declaration where the shareholding chain includes offshore trusts or non-resident entities.
required_dossiers: Form NZ 7 – Registered Office and Address for Service
Form NZ 8 – Appointment of Directors
Signed consent to act for each officer
Ultimate Beneficial Ownership declaration
Registered office landlord or agent written consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected for incomplete particulars, the Company must amend and resubmit within 5 working days to avoid late-filing penalties. In the event of a dispute over officer identity, the Registrar may require a statutory declaration under s 19 Companies Act 1993 before accepting the filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Non-Industrial Compliance, Game Classification and Occupational Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of Film and Literature Classification (Te Mana Whakaatu), Wellington; Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ); WorkSafe New Zealand.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For a digital software publisher under ISIC 5820, no manufacturing or environmental operating permit is required. Submit the MMORPG title for voluntary classification to obtain a G, PG, M, R13, R16 or R18 rating for lawful retail and advertising in New Zealand, and implement Privacy Act 2020 data-handling and breach-notification procedures covering in-app purchase profiles. For the leased registered office, secure a fire safety certificate and evacuation scheme from FENZ, a building warrant of fitness if the premises are open to the public, and a WorkSafe health-and-safety induction for all staff.
required_dossiers: MMORPG classification application and demo build
Privacy Act 2020 compliance policy and privacy officer appointment
FENZ fire evacuation scheme or certificate
Building Warrant of Fitness (where applicable)
WorkSafe New Zealand health-and-safety induction records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Classification Office assigns a higher rating than anticipated, the Company may commission an independent classification opinion and resubmit. Any FENZ deficiency notice must be rectified within the specified compliance period; a temporary occupancy certificate may be sought from the territorial authority while corrective works are completed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for ISIC 5820 (software publishing); the only content-related authority is the Office of Film and Literature Classification (Te Mana Whakaatu), Wellington, New Zealand, operating under the Films, Videos, and Publications Classification Act 1993.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory manufacturing or industrial operating permit is required. Optional: classification label (G / PG / M / R13 / R16 / R18) issued by the Classification Office for lawful sale, distribution and advertising of the MMORPG in New Zealand; no Software Publisher Exemption Certificate exists under New Zealand law.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (Te Mana Rauhī Taiao), New Zealand – not engaged for a digital-only publisher with no physical development.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – no EIA required as the Company's operations are zero-emission software publishing with no land disturbance, discharge to air, water or land, and no activity listed under the Resource Management Act 1991 requiring a consent.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater, VOC, or particulate discharge applies to digital publishing. Office operations must comply with the Waste Minimisation Act 2008 for e-waste disposal, and general occupational exposure and smoke-free standards under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 for any leased premises.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) fire safety certificate and evacuation scheme for the registered office; building warrant of fitness under the Building Act 2004 where premises are open to the public; WorkSafe New Zealand workplace health-and-safety induction and clearance for all personnel; no special civil-defense or emergency-management obligations for purely digital MMORPG publishing operations beyond the standard FENZ code compliance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), Government of New Zealand — online portal: myIR (https://www.ird.govt.nz/myir)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident/exempted company not carrying on a taxable activity in New Zealand may apply for an IRD number using Form IR742 (Application for IRD number for a non-resident company). The application must be accompanied by certified incorporation documents, a signed declaration of directors and registered office, and, where relevant, evidence of a financial institution account. The application is submitted to Inland Revenue; if the company later registers for GST under the remote services rules, the IRD number is the functional TIN used for electronic returns and myIR enrolment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone (the entity is a non-resident International Company incorporated in a tax-exempt jurisdiction, e.g. Cook Islands; it remains outside New Zealand income tax except to the extent that a New Zealand taxable activity, branch or source income exists; no New Zealand sourced digital game revenue is derived from New Zealand customers unless a fixed establishment or taxable activity arises in New Zealand)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not maintain a US-style check-the-box election. Available targeted elections include: (i) non-resident company election for approved issuer levy (AIL) at 2% on interest payable on qualifying debt, instead of non-resident withholding tax; (ii) election to file a consolidated tax return for wholly-owned NZ-resident company groups (not applicable to non-resident exempt vehicles); and (iii) hybrid mismatch elections/offsetting adjustments under the Hybrid and Mismatch Rules (Subpart FH of the Income Tax Act 2007). None of these alter the entity's Tax_Exempt_Zone classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) — a value added tax administered under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 (annual taxable supplies of goods and services in New Zealand; the same NZD 60,000 threshold applies to non-resident remote-services suppliers, including sellers of electronic/digital services and marketplace operators, under the GST Act).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand does not impose a real-time fiscal clearance, API clearance, or digital stamping mandate for GST invoices. E-invoicing is voluntary and interoperable through the PEPPOL network under the New Zealand Peppol authority managed by Inland Revenue. Standard GST tax invoices issued for zero-rated exports require the supplier's name and GST number, invoice issue date, description of supply, amount, and a clear indication that the supply is zero-rated.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: An exported supply of goods is zero-rated if the goods are exported from New Zealand within 28 days of invoice, payment, or delivery; for services, including digital MMORPG content and in-app purchases supplied to non-resident customers, zero-rating applies if the supply is made to a non-resident outside New Zealand, is not materially connected with land or tangible goods in New Zealand, and is not physically performed in New Zealand. Where sales are executed through marketplace payout rails such as Apple App Store or Google Play, the marketplace operator generally accounts for New Zealand GST on NZ-consumer supplies, while the offshore developer's supply to the marketplace operator itself may qualify for zero-rating as a B2B service to a non-resident.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration / automated export entry (where physical goods are exported)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill showing New Zealand port/airport of departure and overseas destination
Commercial GST tax invoice marked 'zero-rated' (with supplier name, IRD/GST number, invoice date and supply description)
Non-resident customer evidence: IP geolocation record, billing address, bank or wallet payment location, customer registration data
Payment settlement proof: verified PSP payout statement, SWIFT/Telegraphic Transfer confirmation, or inward remittance certificate where FX repatriation is used
Foreign currency conversion or hedging record, where applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue may audit zero-rated export claims retrospectively. If statutory zero-rating criteria are not satisfied, GST is clawed back at 15%, with use-of-money interest from the original filing date. Civil shortfall penalties escalate from 20% (unacceptable tax position) to 40% (gross carelessness) and up to 150% (abusive tax position or evasion); knowingly making false export substantiation constitutes evasion under the Tax Administration Act 1994 and may lead to criminal fines, director/promoter exposure, and imprisonment. Early voluntary disclosure significantly mitigates these penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua) is the apex monetary authority; the Overseas Investment Office (OIO), operating within Land Information New Zealand (LINZ), administers capital-flow screening under the Overseas Investment Act 2005; the New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) supervises AML/CFT reporting for cash and wire movements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The New Zealand dollar (NZD) is fully freely convertible pursuant to New Zealand's acceptance of Article VIII of the IMF Articles of Agreement; no exchange-control restrictions impede current-account or capital-account transactions. Profit remittance is unrestricted for non-resident shareholders, subject only to Non-Resident Withholding Tax (NRWT) at treaty-resident rates (typically 5% on dividends and 10% on royalties/interest under applicable DTTs) or Approved Issuer Levy (AIL) for qualifying offshore borrowing. The only material regulatory gate is the Overseas Investment Act 2005: mandatory consent is triggered for non-resident acquisitions of significant business assets (NZD 100 million or more) or of sensitive land. A passive offshore International Company holding intellectual property and receiving global app-store payouts, with no NZ land or significant asset acquisition, faces negligible convertibility friction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: New Zealand imposes no statutory surrender, mandatory conversion, or repatriation timeline on export proceeds. Exporters and digital-content licensors may retain foreign currency indefinitely in offshore or domestic foreign-currency accounts. Compliance obligations are limited to (i) RBNZ Balance of Payments statistical reporting at de minimis survey thresholds, and (ii) AML/CFT reporting by reporting entities for wire transfers or cash transactions exceeding NZD 10,000. No exchange-rate conversion ratio or time limit is prescribed by law.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW for primary settlement treasury accounts; MEDIUM-HIGH for ancillary rails only. Offshore digital EMIs (UK FCA e-money institutions, EU EMIs, or Singapore/ Hong Kong digital banks) do not enjoy passporting rights into New Zealand and are not recognised as registered banks under the Banking (Prudential Supervision) Act 1989. To touch NZ-dollar settlement rails they must register on the Financial Service Providers Register (FSPR) under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008 and obtain an AML/CFT compliance programme under the AML/CFT Act 2009 as a money or value transfer service (MVTS). In practice, a CK_IC treasury structure should use an NZ Tier-1 bank as the legal-entity operational account and use EMIs solely for FX conversion, virtual card issuance, or merchant payouts to remote contractors; the final settlement leg must land in the NZ bank account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no statutory requirement for directors to appear physically in New Zealand. Under the AML/CFT Act 2009 Customer Due Diligence rules, Tier-1 banks may accept remote onboarding using electronic identity verification (eID) and video-conference interviews. However, in practice, for a tax-exempt offshore International Company (CK_IC) with non-resident beneficial owners, most NZ banks require either (i) a physical or video interview with all directors and beneficial owners, or (ii) a certification of identity issued by an NZ-licensed chartered accountant, lawyer, or notary public, together with a live verification call. Purely automated, zero-human-signoff onboarding is routinely declined; at least one authorised signatory with an NZ nexus (registered office address, resident agent, or local director) is strongly recommended.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-exempt offshore International Company flag: CK_IC domiciled in a no-tax jurisdiction, perceived as a classic offshore shell with opaque beneficial ownership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full beneficial-ownership (BO) attestation form; certified certificate of incorporation and overseas company registration in New Zealand (if registered as an overseas company under the Companies Act 1993); certified register of directors and shareholders; trust deed or foundation deed where ownership is layered; registered agent certificate of good standing; board resolution explaining the commercial purpose (global MMORPG publishing and IP licensing); and a source-of-funds declaration for every ultimate beneficial owner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: No economic substance: no employees, no physical office, no audited financial statements in New Zealand.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Economic substance package comprising an NZ registered office and service address; management-services agreement with an NZ-registered corporate services provider; substance declaration confirming decision-making occurs in NZ; two years of GAAP-compliant financial statements (or a reviewed opening balance sheet); transaction flow chart evidencing real commercial functions (Apple/Google platform contracts, contractor payments, user-support outsourcers); and evidence of IP development activities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume digital revenue with atypical invoicing: large, frequent Apple App Store / Google Play payouts, no paper trail, high customer-location diversity, and possible perceived nexus to online-gaming money laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original developer agreements (Apple Developer Program License Agreement; Google Play Distribution Agreement); monthly payout reconciliation reports from Apple and Google; a pro-forma revenue forecast; sample customer refund- and chargeback policy; compliance certification confirming no virtual-currency cash-out or player-to-player trading; and clear segregation of treasury inflows (platform payouts) from operational outflows (royalties, contractors, tax payments).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP, and adverse-media overlap: beneficial owner or jurisdiction appears on negative news outputs or sanctions-adjacent databases.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent sanctions and PEP screening report from a recognised provider (World-Check, Refinitiv, Dow Jones) dated within 90 days; sworn declarations of non-PEP status for all directors, ultimate beneficial owners and senior managers; nationality, tax-residency certificates for each UBO; adverse-media explanation letters with primary-source rebuttals; and an AML/CFT compliance manual adopted by the entity.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections from the parent or beneficial owner must be executed via SWIFT MT103/MT202 creditor-institution transfers using ISO 15022/20022 purpose codes: for equity subscription use purpose code 'C6' (Investment in a subsidiary in the receiving country) or 'T1'; for intercompany loans use 'T2' (Other capital transfers) with a signed intercompany loan agreement bearing arm's-length interest. The NZ receiving bank requires: (i) a board resolution approving the share allotment or loan drawdown; (ii) a share register update or loan agreement; (iii) Non-Resident Withholding Tax declaration (RW-NRWT or AIL election for interest); and (iv) a source-of-funds disclosure for amounts above NZD 10,000. Clearance settles same-day via the RBNZ Exchange Settlement Account System (ESAS) in AUD for the NZ leg; FX conversion into NZD or USD may be transacted at bank-treasury rates, and the entire flow must be entered on the entity's capital/loan schedule for OIO and IRD record purposes. Apportioned purpose code 'B2' (Other royalties and license fees) is prohibited for equity injections.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational disbursements—royalties to IP sub-licensors, software-development subcontractors, cloud hosting fees, and marketing-agency payments—clear primarily via SWIFT MT103 single remittances or MT102 batch files with income purpose codes (Category C: 'Royalties and license fees', 'Software royalties', 'Fees for services'), accompanied by invoices, tax invoices, or statements. For large B2B content-development agreements, a Commercial Letter of Credit (UCP 600) opened via MT700, with documents-against-payment (D/P) terms, provides bank-confirmed settlement and mitigates counterparty risk; standby LCs may collateralise platform performance obligations. Domestic NZD disbursements use the Bulk Electronic Clearing System (BECS) and single-authority OIO (low value) rails; all outbound transfers above NZD 10,000 generate FIU reporting and must be tagged with the correct NZ IRD/FIU narrative to avoid compliance holds. There is no requirement to route app-store payouts through any LC or collection mechanism, as those are inbound from Apple/Google treasury via their proprietary payout rails.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla deliverable FX forwards (NZD/USD, NZD/EUR, NZD/GBP, NZD/AUD, NZD/CNH) with an authorised NZ dealing bank under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, maturities up to 24 months, booked under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on non-fully-convertible emerging-market currencies (e.g., CNY/CNH, INR, IDR, PHP, VND) referencing offshore fixing rates, used solely to hedge Chinese, Indian, and Southeast Asian contractor/supplier cost baskets
Cross-currency swaps (NZD/USD and NZD/EUR) to re-denominate intercompany shareholder loans and equalise asset-liability currency exposure on the consolidated balance sheet

European-style vanilla FX options (puts and calls) on NZD/USD to protect large semi-annual Apple/Google payout conversion cycles, with no exotic barrier features absent a registered derivatives issuer

Upset-rate collar and participating swap structures, permissible only where the counterparty is a registered bank or licensed derivatives issuer under the FMC Act 2013; no cryptocurrency, crypto-derivative or decentralised-finance hedging instruments are permitted for treasury purposes

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return of a New Zealand Company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office (MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 working days after the anniversary of the date of incorporation (return date is the last day of the preceding month on the anniversary)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers an infringement fee of NZD 137 (approx USD 84); if the return remains overdue after a formal default/removal notice (minimum 20 working days), the Registrar may remove the company from the Companies Register and directors face offence fines up to NZD 50,000.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Financial statements (for companies not exempt from general purpose financial reporting, i.e., entities exceeding small-company thresholds)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office (MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Financial statements must be completed, signed, and circulated to shareholders within 5 months after the balance date; subsequently filed with the Companies Office within 20 working days of the circulation/signing date where applicable.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file audited financial statements without reasonable excuse is an offence punishable by a fine not exceeding NZD 50,000 for the company and NZD 5,000 for each director (plus ongoing daily penalties if court-ordered).

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent audit is mandatory for a New Zealand company unless it qualifies as 'small' under the Financial Reporting Act 2013. A company is large (and therefore must be audited) if, in both of the two preceding consecutive accounting periods, it exceeds any one of the following on a consolidated group basis where applicable: (i) total assets NZD 5.5 million; (ii) total revenue NZD 11 million; (iii) more than 25 full-time-equivalent employees.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: NZ GAAP as promulgated by the External Reporting Board (XRB) — comprising NZ IFRS for large for-profit entities, the Reduced Disclosure Regime (RDR) for moderate-sized entities, and NZ FRS for SMEs for eligible smaller companies.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand has no separate annual UBO return for an ordinary registered company; ownership changes are recorded in the Register of Members and reflected in the Annual Return filed with the Companies Office. For AML/CFT purposes, the registered agent or incorporated secretary must carry out beneficial-owner verification at the time of any material shareholding change and retain the verification records (including UBO data) for at least 5 years after the relationship ends.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: NZD 800–2,500 per year (approx USD 500–1,550) for registered office, company secretarial, and registered agent services from a licensed New Zealand services provider.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: NZD 5,000–15,000 per year (approx USD 3,100–9,300) for a basic New Zealand statutory audit; higher for a global MMORPG operation requiring consolidated, multi-jurisdiction revenue audit support.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holiday is available under the Income Tax Act 2007. The principal incentive is the Research and Development Tax Incentive at 15% of eligible R&D expenditure, refundable in cash at the 15% credit rate for qualifying loss-making companies subject to statutory caps. The imputation system attaches imputation credits to distributions, preventing economic double taxation for New Zealand-resident shareholders. A non-resident International Company with no New Zealand permanent establishment is assessable only on New Zealand-sourced income; foreign-sourced income is exempt. The tax classification model Tax_Exempt_Zone applies only where the entity is a foreign company that is not resident in New Zealand and derives no New Zealand-source income.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (indefinite carry-forward), subject to the 49% shareholder continuity rule and, where continuity is between 49% and 66%, the business continuity test; there is no statutory 5-year expiration under New Zealand law.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 - Company Income Tax Return; submitted electronically through the Inland Revenue myIR secure portal or via IRD-approved tax agent software
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For the standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 is due on 7 July (two months after balance date). Where a registered tax agent has an extension of time, the filing date for a 31 March balance date is deferred to 31 March of the following year. For non-standard balance dates, the return is due on the 28th day of the fourth month after balance date, or with a tax agent extension on the 28th day of the sixth month after balance date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross business income: worldwide gross revenue derived from MMORPG operations, including Apple App Store and Google Play in-app purchase payouts, virtual currency sales, subscriptions and ancillary digital services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident International Company must report only New Zealand-sourced gross business income here; income sourced outside New Zealand from foreign game users is not assessable and should be excluded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total income: aggregate of business income, interest, dividends and other assessable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies must include only income that is sourced in New Zealand under the Income Tax Act 2007, such as payments made by New Zealand resident game users or attributable to a New Zealand permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income (or net loss): total assessable income less deductible expenses, including platform commissions, development costs, server hosting, marketing and administrative expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses are deductible only to the extent they are incurred in deriving New Zealand-sourced assessable income; apportionment is required for globally interlinked costs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income: net income after deducting any carried-forward losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident company may utilise carried-forward losses only if it satisfies the continuity of ownership and same-business tests; losses incurred before becoming non-resident require special compliance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax on taxable income: computed at the 28% company rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident International Companies are assessed at the same 28% rate on taxable New Zealand-source income; the tax-exempt status of an offshore jurisdiction does not eliminate New Zealand tax on New Zealand-source digital revenues.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of NZ$250 per month or part-month for which the IR4 is outstanding, with additional penalties at the discretion of the Commissioner. Late payment penalties comprise an initial 1% of unpaid tax plus an incremental 4% penalty charged on the 7th day of each subsequent month of non-payment; use-of-money interest accrues on all unpaid/underpaid tax at a rate of approximately 8.5% per annum.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders; reduced to 15% for portfolio shareholders and 5% for non-resident companies holding at least 10% of the voting power under most New Zealand double tax agreements, including the US-NZ and Australia-NZ DTAs.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply the reduced treaty withholding rate, the non-resident shareholder must provide the New Zealand paying company with a current Certificate of Residence (TRC) issued by the tax authority of the treaty jurisdiction and complete Inland Revenue form IR 281D (Statement for Reduced NRWT Rate). The payer must retain the certificate and declaration as audit evidence before applying the treaty rate; absent valid documentation, the domestic 30% NRWT must be withheld and remitted to Inland Revenue.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic NRWT: 15% on interest and 15% on royalties. Interest may be reduced to 0% NRWT where the payer elects to pay the 2% Approved Issuer Levy (AIL) on qualifying debenture interest. Under modern New Zealand DTAs, interest is generally capped at 10% and royalties at 5%–10%; for example, the US-NZ DTA provides 10% on interest and 5% on royalties, while the Australia-NZ DTA provides a 10% royalty ceiling.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation (Local File and Master File) is mandatorily required where the aggregate value of cross-border related-party transactions exceeds NZ$10 million in an income year. Country-by-Country Reporting applies to multinational groups with consolidated annual group revenue exceeding NZ$1.125 billion. Even below the NZ$10 million threshold, the Commissioner may require documentation where transfer pricing risk indicators are present.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not maintain a standalone Economic Substance Regulations statute, but the doctrine is given effect through the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (s BG 1, Income Tax Act 2007), the arm's-length transfer pricing rules, the anti-hybrid mismatch rules, and the permanent establishment attribution rules. A shell International Company with no real presence, no commercial substance, and no decision-making function will have its affairs recharacterised, and the Commissioner may disregard the separate legal personality for tax purposes where the dominant purpose is obtaining a tax advantage.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Fraudulent Under-Reporting of Digital Revenue
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting or under-declaring gross revenue from Apple App Store and Google Play MMORPG in-app purchases in the IR4, creating false invoices, operating dual accounting systems, or falsely claiming deductible expenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penal tax of 150% of the tax shortfall (Tax Administration Act 1994, s 141E); criminal conviction carrying a fine of up to NZ$50,000 for an individual and NZ$250,000 for a body corporate plus imprisonment for up to five years (s 143B); use-of-money interest is charged on all outstanding amounts; asset restraint and forfeiture proceedings can also be initiated under the Criminal Proceeds (Recovery) Act 2009.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, shadow directors and officers who direct, authorise or knowingly participate in evasion are personally liable for the company's unpaid tax liabilities under the director recovery provisions; they face individual criminal prosecution, travel bans, disqualification from managing corporations, and imprisonment for up to five years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Abusive Tax Avoidance Arrangement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the International Company as a tax-favoured shell or conduit with no commercial substance, no physical presence in New Zealand, no local economic activity, and contrived cross-border related-party transactions engineered solely to exploit tax-exempt status, shift profits out of New Zealand, or obtain treaty shopping benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The General Anti-Avoidance Rule voids the tax advantage and the Commissioner recharacterises the arrangement; a shortfall penalty of 100% of the tax shortfall applies for an abusive tax position (TAA s 141D); treaty relief may be denied under limitation-of-benefit or main-purpose clauses; the company may be deregistered under the Companies Act 1993 and its director disqualified.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly structure or operate the shell company face personal liability for the tax shortfall and penalties under the director penalty regime; they may also be subjected to civil penalties, travel bans, and, in aggravated cases involving dishonest conduct, imprisonment for aiding tax avoidance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Non-Compliance and Profit Shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare and retain contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation where related-party cross-border transactions exceed the NZ$10 million threshold; setting inter-company royalties, service fees, interest, or profit mark-ups that deviate from the arm's length principle, thereby artificially depressing assessable New Zealand income of the MMORPG publisher.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Inland Revenue may amend the taxable income to align with the arm's length standard under the transfer pricing rules, impose shortfall penalties up to 100% of the tax shortfall for avoidance, apply use-of-money interest, and penalise failure to file correct tax returns; Country-by-Country and Master File failures can trigger additional infringement notices and fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve or sign false transfer pricing documentation, or knowingly cause the company to understate taxable profit, are exposed to personal liability for corporate tax debts under the director liability provisions, and to prosecution for making false statements or omitting material particulars, with consequent fines, travel bans, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism (AML/CFT) Non-Compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating unregistered or non-compliant financial services related to the game's payment rails—for example, issuing stored value/e-money, operating proprietary virtual currency exchanges redeemable for fiat currency, or processing customer funds—without implementing AML/CFT obligations under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalties up to NZ$5 million for body corporates and NZ$500,000 for individuals per contravention; money laundering offences under the Crimes Act 1961 carry imprisonment up to seven years; regulatory enforcement orders, public warnings, injunctions, and forced deregistration of the financial service provider may also be imposed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of an AML/CFT-reporting entity that fails to conduct customer due diligence, report suspicious transactions, or maintain prescribed records can be personally fined and imprisoned; senior management may be subject to individual civil penalty proceedings and employment or professional disqualification.
